_README: TERM-018 / RM-N15 - the durable record of WHICH GUARDS HAVE BEEN OBSERVED RED
BEFORE GREEN. Read tests/test_term018_every_guard_can_fire.py; it is the rail
that verifies every line of this file and the reason this file cannot be a
spelling check.
THE GUARD POPULATION IN `derived_population` IS NOT LISTED HERE. It is DERIVED
by AST from the sink module named below, every run. This file only says which
of the derived guards carry an observation and which are declared debt, and the
rail asserts that partition is EXACTLY the derived set. A guard added to the
code and to neither list fails the rail BY NAME on its first run.
WHAT AN `observed` ENTRY MUST SURVIVE (all eight, every run, no exceptions):
1. `predicate.file` + `predicate.scope` resolve to a real def by AST.
2. `predicate.pinned` is PRESENT in that scope's source, after comments and
docstrings are stripped and whitespace normalised.
3. `predicate.mutation` is ABSENT from that same stripped source.
4. DISCRIMINATOR: applying the mutation to the source IN MEMORY makes 2 and 3
both fail. This is what stops a pin that cannot tell the two apart.
5. every `observed_by` node id EXISTS by AST and is COLLECTED by pytest, and
its module mentions - in code, never in a docstring - a name that reaches
the pinned scope.
6. `proof.commit` is an ancestor of HEAD and its message contains
`proof.quote` verbatim. So a record cannot be added without a commit that
records a real red count.
7. `wire` says how the guard is reached in a running process, and it is
checked by AST: a `chain` of real call sites, each name BOUND to the
previous hop's module by an import, ending in a module a Railway service
boots - and every hop is CUT in memory and the chain must break. A `table`
is two such chains with the one runtime lookup between them named in
`unfollowable`; a `sink` and a `cli` are checked for being what they claim.
8. no parameter default in the guard's reach is a def, class or import bound
when the module loads - an injected seam is `=None`, resolved in the body.
WHAT THIS FILE DOES NOT PROVE: that the recorded test is red TODAY if the guard
is reverted. Nothing static can prove that. It proves the mutation was really
performed once, on a named commit, against a named test that still exists and
is still collected, and that the exact predicate it was performed against is
still the predicate in the code.
`declared_unobserved` IS DEBT AND MAY ONLY SHRINK. The ceiling is a literal in
the rail, not in this file, so growing it is a visible test edit.

derived_population._what: The chart-health operator alert channel - lane A's channel (TERM-011).
derived_population._unit: One guard = one emit call site, keyed <relpath>::<enclosing qualname>::<alert key>::<severity>, plus the sink module's own decision functions (`emit` and the same-module functions it calls). The key/severity in the id is the audit's own unit: 'two tiers of one metric under two thresholds are two guards, because they have two predicates'. A computed key or severity reads <computed>.
derived_population._alias_resolution_is_load_bearing: api/services/bars_continuous_audit.py binds the sink as `_alerts` in a FUNCTION-LOCAL import, and its four sites include both intraday_hotset_stale tiers. A derivation matching only the literal name `chart_health_alerts` misses them. This note used to end '- tests/test_chart_health_severity_vocabulary.py does': TRUE WHEN WRITTEN, FALSE NOW, that rail was fixed to resolve aliases scope-aware and pins its population at 21 literal-severity sites.

observed.what_the_guard_decides: Whether a wisdom job that has stopped succeeding pages. The window came from `max(last_ok, boot)` with boot set at module import, so for the one case the guard exists for - a FAILING job, whose last success predates this pod - the age it compared was POD UPTIME. 70 days of uninterrupted uptime for the monthly packet; 30 minutes even for the 900s jobs, above this pod's median life. The predicate is `_staleness_window`, which is a different function from the emit site it governs - that is why this record pins a scope rather than the call site.

declared_unobserved.why: THREE audit rows collapse to ONE derived guard here: the key AND the severity are both computed, so nothing static can split the milestone / ordinary-expiring / expired tiers apart. Splitting the id needs the emitter to pass literals. Also cannot fire on a clock before ~2027-07-04.

The predicate is satisfiable (tests/theme_engine/test_propagation.py) but NOTHING in this repo writes taxonomy_version into a push payload, so the production input is out of reach here. RE-CHECKED 2026-10-10 (lane f-l6): a test CAN build the input with no production change (a payload carrying a taxonomy_version that differs from the seeded one, or a POST to /api/push with PUSH_SECRET), so red-before-green is takeable. What blocks the record is clause 7: the guard is reached only from the /api/push route handler, and a FastAPI route is mounted by include_router and dispatched by the framework, which none of the closed WIRE_KINDS (chain, table, sink, cli) can express. Recording it needs a ruling to add a route wire kind to the rail, not more tests.

tests/test_ai_search_resilience.py asserts key and severity. One-sided. WIRE (checked 2026-10-10, lane f-l6): every scheduled caller registers a LAMBDA (`add_job(lambda: _ais_brief_run(...))`, api/main.py ai_search_briefings jobs) through an ALIASED from-import, and the request-path callers end at `include_router`; clause 7 can follow neither, so a red-before-green test alone could not be recorded.

No test names the key. WIRE (checked 2026-10-10, lane f-l6): reached from bars_fetch on the request path and by many callers, so no single hop carries it and a cut of any one call would leave the chain intact (clause 7).

classify/should_page are pure and unit-covered; no assertion of the emit itself was found. FIRED AND MUTATION-PROVED 2026-10-10 (lane f-l6, proof 64f32fec6: registry.run_job(wisdom_capture_eod) through the job table; the page demoted to warning reds 3, tests/test_term018_wisdom_guards.py and tests/test_wisdom_capture_runner.py), but NOT recordable: clause 7 wants a table entry named by a literal id at a JobSpec call whose fn is a plain name, and capture/jobs.py builds its six JobSpecs through _cron(families.JOB_*, ...) with fn=_slot(job_id). Recording needs either capture/jobs.py to declare its entries literally (which would restate the families constants) or the rail to follow _cron; a lane call, not a test.
